title: pylint does not install by "easy_install lint" on Anaconda 1.91 Python distribution
body:
Originally reported by: **Rolf Hemmerling (BitBucket: [hemmerling](http://bitbucket.org/hemmerling), GitHub: @hemmerling?)**

---

Hello,
as PyLint is not distributed with the Anaconda 1.91, a Python 2.7.x distribution ( on WIndows 7 in my case )
http://www.continuum.io
, I tried to install PyLint by
"easy_install lint"
which indeed tries to install PyLint ( AFAIK, IMHO ).

Unfortunately the online web installation process is broken,
after several steps, error messages appear which indicate that some of the downloaded and executed code failed due to syntax errors.

As the process of online installation indeed cannot be repeated easily without desintallation of the whole Python distribution ( which might take 1 hour ) and resinstallation of the whole Ptython distribution ( which might take another hour ),
and as the installation process prints both messages on StdOut and StdErr,
which is hard to catch on Windows,

I don´t add any "proofs" for the breaking of the online installation. Sorry.

But you can be shure,
(1) I started with a fresh working "Anaconda 1.9.1" distribution,
(2) "Easy_install" is a proofed shipped installation procedure both on Python x,y and Anaconda, which works with other Python packages ( e.g. "behave" )
(3) I had proper Internet access, as some depending packages were installed
(4) Syntax error messages were printed on the screen
(5) At the end PyLint was not installed :-(

I got feedback by another Python usergroup member
https://groups.google.com/a/continuum.io/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/anaconda/mSQpci3E5Ao
"for testing purposes it contains Python files with invalid syntax, so creating the .pyc files fails"

So if the problem is reproducable easiy, 
so that not just me fails, on Python 2.7 and probably on any platform,
why is such rotten code included in an official downloadable edition of PyLint?

Indeed, fixing installation processes where the code is downloaded from online repositories, is a challenge for Python beginners like me, to be honest, I won´t like to invest time, I would give up.

So I would be pleased about a fix, so that PyLint can be downloaded and installed by Python editions and distributions where it is still missing ( remember any update will ruin my current "Python installation / distribution" and I will end up without Pylint even if it was included in a downloadabe Python distribution ).

Sincerely
Rolf
